correctness.rationale: This is the specified Lebesgue-stationary three-coordinate map and only the observable c-1/2. The four affine images have disjoint interiors covering the cube and unit Jacobian. The full-branch u-map supplies independent itinerary choices of weights (1/4,1/4,1/2) independently of the initial c; splitting the last branch by c simply gives doubling mod 1. This yields the stated central operator. The binary digits are independent fair bits under Lebesgue measure; doubling shifts the Rademacher index up, while the two half maps average to a down shift except at index 1 where they cancel. Thus the walk is killed, not reflected, at 0. Solving the resolvent recurrence with geometric forcing and zero boundary gives the difference of the (1/2)^j and eta^j modes, yielding the stated sum. Substituting z=2 eta/(1+eta^2) simplifies the sum to (1+eta^2)/(3(2-eta)^2), verifying cancellation at 4/5 and giving square-root coefficients -2 sqrt(2) and -2 sqrt(2)/81 at the two edges. Independently, the sine transform diagonalizes the killed half-line transition at cos(t) and gives C_n=(1/(8 pi)) times the integral on [0,pi] of cos(t)^n sin(t)^2/(5/4-cos(t))^2. Laplace expansion at the two ends gives the quoted leading coefficient: the endpoint denominators before squaring are 1/4 and 9/4, hence the ratio 1/81 with sign (-1)^n. The quadratic vanishing and next even Taylor terms give O(n^-5/2); the interior is exponentially small. Exact direct dyadic-cell integration of the branch dynamics (/workspace/review_work/baker.py) produced lags 0..7: 1/12, 1/24, 7/192, 5/192, 73/3072, 115/6144, 859/49152, 355/24576. This diagnostic does not substitute for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The simplest nonconstant smooth central coordinate is a natural test observable for a neutral baker model. A closed all-lag covariance and unequal amplitudes resolve what the optimal order bound cannot: simultaneous contributions from two spectral edges with a measurable parity effect. The scope is a concrete benchmark, not a claim for arbitrary observables or parameters.
